page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.xlarge is a burstable shared-core virtual machine instance configured on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, providing 4 vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU includes 35 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and supports vector instructions such as AVX-512 Foundation and AVX-512 VNNI. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of memory, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It includes zero bundled local storage and has no discrete hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results reflect the shared and burstable CPU scheduling of the t6 platform, with general compute testing placing consistently in the lower performance brackets. The instance scored 983.0 on single-core and 2922.0 on multi-core Geekbench suites, alongside a multi-core stress-ng metric of 5015.63. Memory throughput testing demonstrates an uncached large-block write speed of 26.23 GB/sec, which falls within the middle 50% category, whereas large-block read throughput reached 34.73 GB/sec. Data compression metrics show lower throughput, registering 6.76 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and 13.02 GB/sec in multi-threaded decompression.

Targeted operational benchmarks confirm baseline utility for modest workloads. Redis achieved 4.94 million SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 4.16 GB/sec. Small-model language inference (135M parameters) delivered 234.69 prompt processing tokens per second and 61.81 generation tokens per second. The server maintains cost efficiency for variable loads that spend long intervals idling, though sustained, continuous CPU-intensive processes face burstable throttling constraints.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m4.xlarge is suitable for low-traffic web applications, non-critical background microservices, staging environments, build queue workers, and small memory-tolerant databases with non-continuous utilization patterns.
